Research markers D/E/F do not add predictive value.\n\nRemaining uncertainty is concentrated in near-threshold or context-specific signals. MYC amplification is associated with slightly weaker WRN dependency at the statistical edge (H189 signed +0.033, interval +0.002 to +0.064), but its lower bound is below the practical WRN threshold; STK11 loss is associated with slightly weaker USP7 dependency at the statistical edge (H190 signed +0.041, interval +0.001 to +0.082), but the lower bound is below the practical USP7 threshold. RB1-loss POLR2A remains inconclusive; KRAS mutation and EGFR amplification main effects remain borderline; CDKN2A-MDM2 in all TP53-loss cells remains unresolved because validation is imprecise, even though the MTAP-intact subset is accepted; MTAP/CDKN2A interaction effects remain unresolved. These are not accepted as clinically meaningful because the interval does not reliably clear the 10% threshold or is too imprecise.\n\nThe most informative next analysis is already active: quantify effect modification of the accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 association by TP53 status (H201), and test whether the near-threshold weaker MYC-amplification WRN association is modified by MYC expression at the median (H202). If only one follow-up is possible, H201 is more valuable because PTEN-STAT3 is a large robust association and the p53-stratum difference may indicate a biologically important context, whereas H202 would likely refine an already borderline signal. No causal interpretation is implied; genetic-marker co-occurrence, copy-number neighborhood effects, and technical batch/library variation remain potential confounders."}}

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed R215-R226 using the signed interval conventions: for direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger dependency, while for direction +1, positive signed estimates indicate weaker dependency. I applied outcome-specific approximate 10-percent practical thresholds, with a conservative interpretation requiring the interval to clear the threshold for accepted clinically meaningful claims. PTEN-loss was again associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency in both PIK3CA-mutant cells (H214/R216: +0.268, +0.127 to +0.409) and PIK3CA-intact cells (H219/R221: +0.267, +0.211 to +0.323), so the PTEN-STAT3 association appears broad across PIK3CA pathway context. The KRAS-mutant interaction test was too imprecise to support a clinically meaningful modification (H213/R215: -0.024, -0.148 to +0.100), as was the high-MYC-expression interaction (H220/R222: +0.031, -0.074 to +0.135); both are closed unresolved. The very strong SMARCA4-loss to stronger SMARCA2-dependency association remained robust in KEAP1-loss cells (H215/R217: +0.787, +0.737 to +0.836) and TP53-intact cells (H217/R219: +0.787, +0.766 to +0.809). The very strong TP53-loss to weaker USP7-dependency association also persisted in STK11-loss cells (H216/R218: +0.825, +0.766 to +0.885). The KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2-dependency association persisted under high hypoxia (H218/R220: +0.754, +0.711 to +0.797). MSI-high status remained associated with much stronger WRN dependency in high-ploidy cells (H221/R223: +0.771, +0.728 to +0.814), and CDKN2A loss remained associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in low-MYC-expression cells (H222/R224: +0.129, +0.058 to +0.199). EGFR amplification did not support clinically meaningful stronger STAT3 dependency in PTEN-intact cells (H223/R225: -0.022, -0.049 to +0.006); this is rejected for the hypothesized clinically meaningful effect. ERBB2 amplification in PTEN-intact cells was statistically supportive of stronger STAT3 dependency (H224/R226: +0.032, +0.003 to +0.061), but its lower bound falls below the approximate STAT3 practical threshold, so it is unresolved closed as suggestive but not confidently clinically meaningful. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal effects or external claims. I registered refinements to test the unresolved PTEN-STAT3 and ERBB2-STAT3 contexts with complementary main-effect analyses and to complete the CDKN2A-MDM2 MYC-expression split.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

record.narrative:
No validation response is due, no new independent validation can be requested, and the newly available context analyses have already been assessed. The evidence now supports the following supplied-dataset associations, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable claims. Using the signed-interval conventions and approximate outcome-specific 10% practical thresholds: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H18/R5/R26, discovery +0.796 and validation +0.781. TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency, H12/R10/R13, discovery +0.802 and validation +0.797. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H7/R7/R39, discovery +0.784 and validation +0.807. MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, H13/R11/R53, discovery +0.790 and validation +0.771. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H117/R108 overall +0.117, with validated TP53-intact evidence H96/R70/R93 around +0.118/+0.122 and many robust co-mutation/copy-number contexts. PTEN loss is associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency, H184/R188 +0.267, with consistent large effects in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, KRAS-wild-type, PIK3CA-mutant, and PIK3CA-intact strata; PTEN-STAT3 remains accepted from discovery but not independently validated.

Important negative findings are broad. Direct target alterations mostly do not predict their own dependency: BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency, H2/H77; KRAS mutation for KRAS dependency, H1/H31/H49/H72, with near-null validation; EGFR amplification for EGFR dependency, H3/H50/H51/H20, with validation in the opposite direction; ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency, H4/H78; and several RTK-related effects on RIT1 dependency, H16/H17/H79/H90/H91/H105/H83. MYC amplification is not supported for stronger POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, KIF18A, or USP7 dependency, H9/H10/H11/H94/H81. RB1 loss is not meaningful for KIF18A or SMARCA2 dependency, H14/H185. Research markers D, E, and F do not provide reliable added predictive value, H144-H148.

Unresolved uncertainty is mostly near-threshold, imprecise, or context-dependent. MYC amplification shows a weak opposite-direction WRN signal near the practical threshold, H189/R186 +0.033, lower bound below threshold. STK11 loss and USP7 dependency is near threshold, H190/R190 +0.041, lower bound below threshold. NF1-loss KRAS dependency remains unresolved in KRAS-wild-type contexts, H68/R54, H69/R55, H70/R56. RB1-loss POLR2A dependency is near threshold but not clinically clear, H169/R173 and related subgroup analyses. ERBB2 amplification in PTEN-intact, EGFR-intact cells is suggestive but below the practical threshold, H224/R226. PTEN-STAT3 interaction by KRAS mutation or high MYC expression is too imprecise, H213/R215 and H220/R222. MTAP/CDKN2A interactions and some TP53-loss CDKN2A-MDM2 validation remain imprecise.

The most informative next analyses are already in the active queue: H225 PTEN-STAT3 among KRAS-mutant cells; H226 PTEN-STAT3 among high-MYC-expression cells; H227 ERBB2-STAT3 among PTEN-intact, EGFR-intact cells; H228 CDKN2A-MDM2 among high-MYC-expression cells. The new registered proposals add robustness tests for the accepted large associations and targeted follow-up of near-threshold signals: PTEN-STAT3 in adenocarcinoma; TP53-USP7 in MTAP-loss cells; SMARCA4-SMARCA2 in PTEN-loss cells; MSI-high-WRN in lower-ploidy cells; CDKN2A-MDM2 in PTEN-loss cells; NF1-loss KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type, TP53-wild-type adenocarcinoma; RB1-loss POLR2A in KRAS-wild-type cells; and KEAP1-NFE2L2 in KRAS-wild-type cells. If forced to prioritize one, H225 is the single most informative because PTEN-STAT3 is a large accepted association and KRAS-pathway context may reveal clinically meaningful effect modification.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore stage registers nine new discovery comparisons. I retain the direction convention used in the ledger: for direction -1, the hypothesis is that the exposed group has more negative, stronger dependency, so the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative; for direction +1, the hypothesis is that the exposed group has less negative, weaker dependency, so the expected raw difference is positive. The first proposal is a novel broad exploration of TMED10 dependency, testing whether EGFR amplification is associated with stronger TMED10 dependency, possibly reflecting trafficking or secretion demands in RTK-amplified cells. The second and third proposals refine previously negative MYC-amplification tests for DHX9 and POLR2A by restricting to cells with high MYC expression; if MYC amplification confers dependency only when the MYC transcriptional program is actually high, the estimates should move away from zero. The fourth tests whether the accepted MSI-high to stronger WRN dependency association persists in SLFN11-high cells, where DNA damage-response biology may reinforce replication-stress dependence. The fifth and sixth test whether the accepted PTEN-loss to stronger STAT3-dependency association remains clinically meaningful in inflammatory IFN-gamma-high and hypoxia-high contexts, both plausible STAT3-relevant stress states. The seventh tests whether the KEAP1-loss to weaker NFE2L2-dependency association persists in high-MYC-expression cells, where redox and metabolic programs may interact with NRF2 pathway activation. The eighth tests whether the very strong SMARCA4-loss to stronger SMARCA2-dependency association remains in high-MYC-expression cells, probing whether MYC-driven proliferation or transcriptional stress modifies SWI/SNF synthetic dependence. The ninth follows up the near-threshold STK11-loss and USP7-dependency signal in high-MYC-expression cells to see whether the effect becomes clearer or attenuates. All comparisons remain association tests in the supplied lung-lineage dataset only. Genetic co-occurrence, copy-number effects, transcriptional-state confounding, batch or library variation, growth-rate differences, and subtype imbalance remain possible explanations.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage requests 12 new discovery analyses from the active untested claim set. The selection completes the highest-priority follow-up queue while adding one novel TMED10 exploration. H225, H226, and H229 test whether the accepted PTEN-loss association with much stronger STAT3 dependency remains clinically meaningful in KRAS-mutant, high-MYC-expression, and adenocarcinoma contexts, respectively; this is important because PTEN-loss had a large discovery effect but no independent validation, and context-specific attenuation would change interpretation. H227 tests ERBB2 amplification and STAT3 dependency in PTEN-intact, EGFR-intact cells to resolve the prior near-threshold suggestive signal. H228 completes the CDKN2A-loss MDM2-dependency MYC-expression split. H230, H231, H232, and H236 test robustness of the strongest accepted associations in biologically or technically distinct strata: TP53-loss USP7 dependency among MTAP-loss cells, SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency among PTEN-loss cells, MSI-high WRN dependency among lower-ploidy cells, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency among KRAS-wild-type cells. H234 and H235 target unresolved near-threshold hypotheses: NF1-loss KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type, TP53-wild-type adenocarcinoma, and RB1-loss POLR2A dependency in KRAS-wild-type cells. H237 is a new broad test of EGFR amplification and TMED10 dependency. For direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate weaker dependency in the exposed group. I will assess Welch 95% intervals, validity cell counts, direction consistency, approximate outcome-specific 10% practical significance thresholds, and whether the findings support broad association versus context-dependent association. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered discovery results using the signed-interval convention. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has more negative dependency, i.e., stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has less negative dependency, i.e., weaker dependency. I judged magnitude against approximately 10% practical thresholds based on the typical scale of each dependency score and required uncertainty not to span null or subthreshold values for acceptance of a clinically meaningful supplied-dataset association. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request was made. PTEN loss remained strongly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency across additional contexts: KRAS-mutant cells H225/R227 estimate +0.249, interval +0.139 to +0.358; high-MYC-expression cells H226/R228 +0.283, +0.211 to +0.354; and adenocarcinoma cells H229/R231 +0.268, +0.206 to +0.330. These are far above the practical threshold and support a broad dataset-specific PTEN-STAT3 association, although it remains not independently validated. CDKN2A loss remained associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in high-MYC-expression cells H228/R230 +0.117, +0.066 to +0.168. KEAP1 loss remained associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KRAS-wild-type cells H236/R237 +0.793, +0.769 to +0.817. Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

expectation

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore stage registers four new context-robustness comparisons to accompany the already active queue H238-H245. I use the ledger convention: for direction -1, the expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, and a positive signed estimate indicates that the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency; direction +1 is not used here. First, PTEN loss has a large accepted association with stronger STAT3 dependency in this dataset (H184/R188), but it lacks independent validation. PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling and STAT3 is a hub in inflammatory and mesenchymal-like stress programs, so I test whether the association persists in high-EMT cells. A large positive signed estimate would support a robust dataset-specific PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency association even in mesenchymal-like contexts; a attenuated estimate would suggest context dependence or that the broad discovery signal is diluted by confounded high-EMT subsets. Second, SMARCA4 loss has a very large validated association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7/R7/R39). High-stemness cells may have greater lineage-plasticity and chromatin-state instability, potentially increasing synthetic lethality with SMARCA2; therefore I test whether this association persists in high-stemness cells. A large positive signed estimate would support technical and biological robustness across chromatin-plasticity states; attenuation would indicate possible confounding by lineage, culture state, or batch. Third, CDKN2A loss has an accepted but threshold-bound association with stronger MDM2 dependency, strongest in TP53-intact cells (H117/R108; H96/R70/R93). I restrict to high-quality screens using screen_roc_auc at or above its median to test whether the signal is screen-quality dependent. A positive signed estimate above practical threshold would support a genuine dataset association less likely driven by noisy screens; a near-null result would make the small positive signals more plausible as residual noise or confounded cell-cycle/copy-number effects. Fourth, RB1 loss and POLR2A dependency is unresolved near threshold across several analyses (H169/R173, H235/R236). Restricting to high-quality screens may reduce assay noise and clarify whether RB1-loss cells have a clinically meaningful increase in POLR2A dependency. If positive and above threshold, it would support follow-up; if still near null, the hypothesis should be rejected as not clinically meaningful in this dataset. These proposals remain association tests in the supplied lung-lineage dataset only and do not support causality or external generalizability. Alternative explanations include genetic co-occurrence, copy-number effects, transcriptional-state confounding, screen batch or library effects, growth-rate differences, and multiple subgroup testing.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate indicates stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate indicates weaker/less negative dependency. I will assess magnitude against roughly 10% practical significance relative to outcome scale, interval exclusion of the null, cell-count validity, and consistency with prior evidence. These are dataset-specific association tests only, not causal or generalizable claims.

record.narrative: I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the signed-direction convention: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker/less negative dependency. I judged acceptance using both statistical precision and practical significance, approximately using a 0.10 absolute dependency-score difference as a clinically meaningful threshold in these CRISPR dependency score scales. I also required cell-count validity and excluded intervals spanning the null. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request was made. H238 and H239 are rejected: MYC-amplification in high MYC-expression cells shows near-null estimates for DHX9 and POLR2A dependency, with intervals crossing zero and magnitudes far below practical significance. H240 is accepted: MSI-high cells with high SLFN11 expression show an enormous increase in WRN dependency, +0.819 [0.780, 0.858], robust and far above threshold, though still a supplied-dataset association and not a causal claim. H241, H242, and H246 are accepted: PTEN loss remains strongly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in IFN-gamma-high, hypoxia-high, and EMT-high contexts, with large estimates and intervals excluding zero. This strengthens the dataset-specific robustness of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency across inflammatory and stress-like expression states, but it remains unvalidated externally and could still reflect correlated biology, copy-number/loss heterozygosity confounding, or selection of more aggressive transcriptomic states. H243 is accepted: KEAP1 loss in high MYC-expression cells is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, +0.809 [0.781, 0.838], consistent with the larger validated KEAP1-NFE2L2 association. H244 and H247 are accepted: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high MYC-expression and high stemness contexts, +0.796 and +0.794 respectively, supporting robustness across selected lineage-plasticity and expression states. H245 is rejected: STK11 loss in high MYC-expression cells gives only +0.053 [-0.004, 0.110], a near-threshold point estimate whose interval includes null and does not support clinically meaningful USP7 dependency. H248 is accepted with caution: CDKN2A loss in high-quality screens is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, +0.132 [0.081, 0.184], consistent with the broader accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 signal and not explained as screen noise alone, although this particular subgroup is not independently validated. H249 is rejected: RB1 loss in high-quality screens is near-null for POLR2A dependency, +0.032 [-0.005, 0.070], so high-quality screen restriction does not rescue this association. Overall, these new analyses reinforce the large internal dataset associations (KEAP1-NFE2L2, TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, PTEN-STAT3, CDKN2A-MDM2) while failing to support smaller MYC-expression or high-quality-screen refinements for DHX9, POLR2A, USP7, or RB1-related dependencies. All conclusions are association-level claims within this supplied lung-lineage dataset; multiplicity, genetic co-occurrence, transcriptomic-state confounding, copy-number effects, screen-batch effects, and other residual confounders remain plausible for smaller effects.

record.narrative:
No validation response is due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so there is no new validation to assess and no new validation request can be made. I reassessed a selected set of unresolved near-null associations and changed them to reject and closed because their signed 95% intervals are well below the approximate 0.10 dependency-score practical threshold used throughout this run, even where some intervals excluded zero. These are decisions about scientific and practical meaningfulness in the supplied dataset, not about whether tiny statistical contrasts exist.

Supported dataset-specific associations. Direction convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has weaker, less negative dependency. The strongest supported associations are very large and, for four major axes, independently validated. First, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H18/R5/R26, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.80, and this holds across many internal contexts including adenocarcinoma H56/R41 and high MYC expression H243/R244. Second, TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency, H12/R10/R13, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.80, and with support across several contexts including adenocarcinoma H25/R22, CDKN2A-loss H131/R126, and research_signature_c contexts H166/R170. Third, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H7/R7/R39, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.78 to +0.81, and robustness across ARID1A states, batch, non-Avana library, high MYC expression, high EMT, high stemness, and other strata such as H244/R245 and H247/R248. Fourth, MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency, H13/R11/R53, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.77 to +0.79, and robustness in adenocarcinoma H24/R23/R40 and SLFN11-high cells H240/R241. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H117/R108, with the strongest and most repeated internal support in TP53-intact cells, H96/R70/R93, around +0.12 in discovery and validation, and replicated in several strata including MTAP-intact cells H113/R102, adenocarcinoma H98/R83, low copy_number_9p21 H127/R122, high MYC expression H228/R230, and PTEN-loss cells H207/R209. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency, H184/R188, estimate about +0.27, and this association is internally robust across many contexts, including TP53-intact H187/R191, TP53-loss H188/R192, KRAS-wild-type H206/R208, KRAS-mutant H225/R227, PIK3CA-mutant H214/R216, PIK3CA-intact H219/R221, high MYC expression H226/R228, adenocarcinoma H229/R231, high IFN-gamma H241/R242, high hypoxia H242/R243, and high EMT H246/R247. PTEN-STAT3 is accepted as a supplied-dataset association, but unlike the four very large axes it lacks independent validation, so its external or mechanistic interpretation remains more uncertain.

Negative and unsupported findings. Direct target alterations generally do not predict their own dependency scores in this dataset. BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency, H2/R2 and H77/R60. KRAS mutation is not meaningfully associated with KRAS dependency, H1/R1 and validated near-null H49/R80. EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with EGFR dependency, H3/R3, and related validations or context restrictions do not rescue it, including H51/R133. ERBB2 amplification is not meaningfully associated with ERBB2 dependency, H4/R4, H78/R61, and H17/R144. MYC amplification is not supported for clinically meaningful dependency in POLR2A H9/R9, RPL11 H10/R116 and expression-restricted H133/R128, DHX9 H11/R142, KIF18A H94/R77 and H132/R127, USP7 H81/R132, or WRN; the opposite-direction WRN signal H189/R186 and high-expression refinement H191/R193 are far below practical threshold. RB1 loss is not meaningfully associated with KIF18A H14/R12, SMARCA2 H185/R189, or POLR2A H169/R173, H176/R180, H177/R181, and H235/R236. The constructed research markers D, E, and F do not show reliable predictive value in the targeted tests, H144/R148, H145/R149, H146/R150, H147/R151, and H148/R152, and interaction tests with these markers remain near null. Many smaller associations that were statistically detectable but far below practical importance are now rejected: NF1-loss KRAS-dependency signals in KRAS-wild-type contexts H68/R54, H69/R55, and adenocarcinoma H70/R56 are too small and inconsistent with broader attenuation H67/R66; ERBB2 amplification with STAT3 dependency in PTEN- or EGFR-intact cells H224/R226 and H227/R229 is far below threshold; STK11 loss with USP7 dependency H190/R190 is below threshold; and near-null expression-restricted MYC and RB1 comparisons are unsupported. These results argue against overinterpreting small, context-specific or nominally significant contrasts.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mostly where effects are near threshold, imprecise, or dependent on small cell counts. CDKN2A loss with MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells is borderline and not firm, H108/R97/R106. CDKN2A-loss effects in high copy_number_9p21 contexts H111/R100 and H120/R111, in batch-restricted TP53-intact cells H110/R99, and in MTAP interaction models H114/R103 and H121/R112 remain unresolved because of small exposed cells, wide intervals, or inconsistent directions. I therefore propose median-split or quartile-split tests of the accepted large effects across screen_roc_auc, Cas9 activity, and aneuploidy. Direction convention: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger or more negative dependency in the exposed group, and the anticipated raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker or less negative dependency, and the anticipated raw contrast is positive. The SMARCA4-SMARCA2 tests ask whether the very large synthetic-lethality-like association persists in high-quality screens, high Cas9 activity, and low aneuploidy; persistence would argue against screen-noise, editing-artifact, or copy-number confounding. The TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 tests ask whether the equally large opposite-direction dependencies are robust across high screen quality and either high Cas9 activity or high aneuploidy. The MSI-WRN test asks whether the large MSI-specific WRN dependency survives high screen quality. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The main supported supplied-dataset associations are KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency especially in TP53-intact cells, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The four largest axes have independent validation, but PTEN-STAT3 does not, and even validated large effects could be sensitive to screen quality, editing efficiency, copy-number burden, or other assay/biology confounders. I therefore propose median-split or quartile-split tests of the accepted large effects across screen_roc_auc, Cas9 activity, and aneuploidy. Direction convention: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger or more negative dependency in the exposed group, and the anticipated raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker or less negative dependency, and the anticipated raw contrast is positive. The SMARCA4-SMARCA2 tests ask whether the very large synthetic-lethality-like association persists in high-quality screens, high Cas9 activity, and low aneuploidy; persistence would argue against screen-noise, editing-artifact, or copy-number confounding. The TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 tests ask whether the equally large opposite-direction dependencies are robust across high screen quality and either high Cas9 activity or high aneuploidy. The MSI-WRN test asks whether the large MSI-specific WRN dependency survives high screen quality. The PTEN-STAT3 tests are especially informative because PTEN-STAT3 is accepted internally but lacks independent validation; high- and low-quality screen splits test assay-quality dependence, while high-Cas9 restriction tests whether editing efficiency explains the association. The CDKN2A-MDM2 test asks whether the strongest biologically interpretable MDM2 effect, restricted to TP53-intact cells, remains strong under high Cas9 activity. If these effects remain large and interval-excluding-null, they strengthen dataset-specific internal robustness. If attenuated near zero, the claims remain association-level but require more caution about technical or genomic confounding; these proposals still do not support causality or external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage requests the 12 highest-value active, untested claims already registered in the ledger: H238-H249. These are dataset-specific association tests only, not causal or generalizable claims.","appraise":"I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the signed-direction convention: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker/less negative dependency. I judged acceptance using both statistical precision and practical significance, approximately using a 0.10 absolute dependency-score difference as a clinically meaningful threshold in these CRISPR dependency score scales. I also required cell-count validity and excluded intervals spanning the null. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request was made. H238 and H239 are rejected: MYC-amplification in high MYC-expression cells shows near-null estimates for DHX9 and POLR2A dependency, with intervals crossing zero and magnitudes far below practical significance. H240 is accepted: MSI-high cells with high SLFN11 expression show an enormous increase in WRN dependency, +0.819 [0.780, 0.858], robust and far above threshold, though still a supplied-dataset association and not a causal claim. H241, H242, and H246 are accepted: PTEN loss remains strongly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency in IFN-gamma-high, hypoxia-high, and EMT-high contexts, with large estimates and intervals excluding zero. This strengthens the dataset-specific robustness of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency across inflammatory and stress-like expression states, but it remains unvalidated externally and could still reflect correlated biology, copy-number/loss heterozygosity confounding, or selection of more aggressive transcriptomic states. H243 is accepted: KEAP1 loss in high MYC-expression cells is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, +0.809 [0.781, 0.838], consistent with the larger validated KEAP1-NFE2L2 association. H244 and H247 are accepted: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in high MYC-expression and high stemness contexts, +0.796 and +0.794 respectively, supporting robustness across selected lineage-plasticity and expression states. H245 is rejected: STK11 loss in high MYC-expression cells gives only +0.053 [-0.004, 0.110], a near-threshold point estimate whose interval includes null and does not support clinically meaningful USP7 dependency. H248 is accepted with caution: CDKN2A loss in high-quality screens is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, +0.132 [0.081, 0.184], consistent with the broader accepted CDKN2A-MDM2 signal and not explained as screen noise alone, although this particular subgroup is not independently validated. H249 is rejected: RB1 loss in high-quality screens is near-null for POLR2A dependency, +0.032 [-0.005, 0.070], so high-quality screen restriction does not rescue this association. Overall, these new analyses reinforce the large internal dataset associations (KEAP1-NFE2L2, TP53-USP7, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, PTEN-STAT3, CDKN2A-MDM2) while failing to support smaller MYC-expression or high-quality-screen refinements for DHX9, POLR2A, USP7, or RB1-related dependencies. All conclusions are association-level claims within this supplied lung-lineage dataset; multiplicity, genetic co-occurrence, transcriptomic-state confounding, copy-number effects, screen-batch effects, and other residual confounders remain plausible for smaller effects.","synthesize":"No validation response is due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so there is no new validation to assess and no new validation request can be made. These are decisions about scientific and practical meaningfulness in the supplied dataset, not about whether tiny statistical contrasts exist.\n\nSupported dataset-specific associations. Direction convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has stronger, more negative dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has weaker, less negative dependency. The strongest supported associations are very large and, for four major axes, independently validated. First, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, H18/R5/R26, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.80, and this holds across many internal contexts including adenocarcinoma H56/R41 and high MYC expression H243/R244. Third, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H7/R7/R39, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.78 to +0.81, and robustness across ARID1A states, batch, non-Avana library, high MYC expression, high EMT, high stemness, and other strata such as H244/R245 and H247/R248. Fourth, MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency, H13/R11/R53, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.77 to +0.79, and robustness in adenocarcinoma H24/R23/R40 and SLFN11-high cells H240/R241. EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with EGFR dependency, H3/R3, and related validations or context restrictions do not rescue it, including H51/R133. Many smaller associations that were statistically detectable but far below practical importance are now rejected: NF1-loss KRAS-dependency signals in KRAS-wild-type contexts H68/R54, H69/R55, and adenocarcinoma H70/R56 are too small and inconsistent with broader attenuation H67/R66; ERBB2 amplification with STAT3 dependency in PTEN- or EGFR-intact cells H224/R226 and H227/R229 is far below threshold; STK11 loss with USP7 dependency H190/R190 is below threshold; and near-null expression-restricted MYC and RB1 comparisons are unsupported. These results argue against overinterpreting small, context-specific or nominally significant contrasts.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mostly where effects are near threshold, imprecise, or dependent on small cell counts. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage requests the 12 currently active, untested confounding/robustness comparisons already registered in the ledger. These are the most informative remaining internal analyses: they test whether the accepted large associations persist under stricter screen-quality, Cas9-editing-efficiency, and genomic-instability/aneuploidy strata. The set covers SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency under high screen_roc_auc, high Cas9 activity, and low aneuploidy; TP53-loss USP7 dependency under high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, and high aneuploidy; KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency under high screen quality and high aneuploidy; MSI-high WRN dependency under high screen quality; PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency under high and low screen quality and high Cas9 activity; and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells under high Cas9 activity. Direction convention remains as before: for direction -1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates indicate weaker/less negative dependency. I will judge results by cell-count validity, interval exclusion of the null, and whether absolute dependency-score differences exceed approximately 0.10. Persistence across these strata would support dataset-specific internal robustness, while attenuation would raise caution about assay noise, editing inefficiency, copy-number burden, or genomic-context confounding. These remain association-level findings in the supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Fourth, MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency, H13/R11/R53, with discovery and validation estimates about +0.77 to +0.79, and robustness in adenocarcinoma H24/R23/R40 and SLFN11-high cells H240/R241. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, H117/R108, with the strongest and most repeated internal support in TP53-intact cells, H96/R70/R93, around +0.12 in discovery and validation, and replicated in several strata including MTAP-intact cells H113/R102, adenocarcinoma H98/R83, low copy_number_9p21 H127/R122, high MYC expression H228/R230, and PTEN-loss cells H207/R209. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency, H184/R188, estimate about +0.27, and this association is internally robust across many contexts, including TP53-intact H187/R191, TP53-loss H188/R192, KRAS-wild-type H206/R208, KRAS-mutant H225/R227, PIK3CA-mutant H214/R216, PIK3CA-intact H219/R221, high MYC expression H226/R228, adenocarcinoma H229/R231, high IFN-gamma H241/R242, high hypoxia H242/R243, and high EMT H246/R247. PTEN-STAT3 is accepted as a supplied-dataset association, but unlike the four very large axes it lacks independent validation, so its external or mechanistic interpretation remains more uncertain.\n\nNegative and unsupported findings. Direct target alterations generally do not predict their own dependency scores in this dataset. BRAF V600E is not meaningfully associated with BRAF dependency, H2/R2 and H77/R60. KRAS mutation is not meaningfully associated with KRAS dependency, H1/R1 and validated near-null H49/R80. EGFR amplification is not meaningfully associated with EGFR dependency, H3/R3, and related validations or context restrictions do not rescue it, including H51/R133. ERBB2 amplification is not meaningfully associated with ERBB2 dependency, H4/R4, H78/R61, and H17/R144. MYC amplification is not supported for clinically meaningful dependency in POLR2A H9/R9, RPL11 H10/R116 and expression-restricted H133/R128, DHX9 H11/R142, KIF18A H94/R77 and H132/R127, USP7 H81/R132, or WRN; the opposite-direction WRN signal H189/R186 and high-expression refinement H191/R193 are far below practical threshold. RB1 loss is not meaningfully associated with KIF18A H14/R12, SMARCA2 H185/R189, or POLR2A H169/R173, H176/R180, H177/R181, and H235/R236. The constructed research markers D, E, and F do not show reliable predictive value in the targeted tests, H144/R148, H145/R149, H146/R150, H147/R151, and H148/R152, and interaction tests with these markers remain near null. Many smaller associations that were statistically detectable but far below practical importance are now rejected: NF1-loss KRAS-dependency signals in KRAS-wild-type contexts H68/R54, H69/R55, and adenocarcinoma H70/R56 are too small and inconsistent with broader attenuation H67/R66; ERBB2 amplification with STAT3 dependency in PTEN- or EGFR-intact cells H224/R226 and H227/R229 is far below threshold; STK11 loss with USP7 dependency H190/R190 is below threshold; and near-null expression-restricted MYC and RB1 comparisons are unsupported. These results argue against overinterpreting small, context-specific or nominally significant contrasts.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mostly where effects are near threshold, imprecise, or dependent on small cell counts. CDKN2A loss with MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss cells is borderline and not firm, H108/R97/R106. CDKN2A-loss effects in high copy_number_9p21 contexts H111/R100 and H120/R111, in batch-restricted TP53-intact cells H110/R99, and in MTAP interaction models H114/R103 and H121/R112 remain unresolved because of small exposed cells, wide intervals, or inconsistent directions. NF1 loss may have a very small residual relationship to KRAS dependency, but it is not clinically meaningful in this dataset; the KRAS-mutant interaction H71/R57 is wide and should not be treated as evidence of biology. Some constructed research signature interactions, such as H151/R155, remain imprecise. RB1-POLR2A and several MYC-related refinements are closed as unsupported near-null. Interactions modifying PTEN-STAT3, including TP53, KRAS, or MYC-expression interactions H201/R203, H213/R215, and H220/R222, are not sufficiently precise to modify the broad PTEN-STAT3 conclusion.\n\nMost informative next analysis. Because independent validation is unavailable, the next most useful work is not more small subgroup mining but confounding and assay-robustness assessment of the few large or accepted unvalidated associations, especially PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. Priority internal analyses would test screen quality and assay metadata: screen_roc_auc, screen_nnmd, cas9 activity, CRISPR library, batch, growth rate, culture type, ploidy, and aneuploidy, plus continuous IFN-gamma, hypoxia, and EMT interactions. Equivalent confirmation for the four very large validated axes using non-Avana library and high-quality-screen restrictions would help determine whether their magnitude is assay-dependent, although they already appear robust. These analyses remain internal and cannot substitute for independent validation. All conclusions are association-level in the supplied lung-lineage dataset. They do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or generalizability beyond this dataset; genetic co-occurrence, copy-number effects, culture or batch structure, screen quality, transcriptional state, and multiple testing remain plausible explanations for smaller effects."}}

record.narrative: Assessing newly delivered discovery evidence with validation capacity exhausted, so no independent validation was requested. I used the signed-direction convention: for direction -1, a positive estimate means stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive estimate means weaker/less negative dependency. I judged scientific and practical meaningfulness using the operational ~0.10 dependency-score-unit threshold used in prior stages, interval exclusion of zero, and valid cell counts. H250-H257 are all accepted and closed: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency remains very large under high screen_roc_auc (+0.791 [0.764,0.819]), high Cas9 activity (+0.791 [0.759,0.823]), and low aneuploidy (+0.799 [0.759,0.838]); TP53-loss USP7 dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.806 [0.780,0.832]) and high Cas9 activity (+0.799 [0.768,0.829]); KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.793 [0.764,0.822]) and high aneuploidy (+0.796 [0.755,0.838]); and MSI-high WRN dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.790 [0.751,0.829]). These do not rescue the associations mechanistically, but they reduce concern that these large supplied-dataset effects are explained by screen noise, low Cas9 editing efficiency, or high copy-number burden alone. H258-H260 are accepted and closed: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is robust to both high and low screen quality and to high Cas9 activity, with estimates +0.253 [0.181,0.325], +0.280 [0.205,0.355], and +0.263 [0.183,0.344]. Because PTEN-STAT3 remains accepted internally but lacks independent validation, this robustness to assay-quality and editing-efficiency strata strengthens it as a dataset-specific association, while still leaving open correlated biology, genetic co-occurrence, copy-number effects, or other residual confounders. H261 is accepted and closed with caution: CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells under high Cas9 activity has point estimate +0.132 [0.068,0.196], above the ~0.10 threshold and excluding zero, although the lower bound is slightly below the threshold. This is consistent with the validated TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 effect and does not support attenuation due to editing inefficiency. All conclusions are association-level in the supplied lung-lineage dataset and do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. Because validation capacity is exhausted, newly registered proposals focus on additional internal confounding/robustness tests of the unvalidated PTEN-STAT3 association and completion of low-aneuploidy strata for two large validated associations.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
