record.narrative: No new validation response is due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so I made no new accept/reject changes. Existing accepted claims remain accepted unless future discovery evidence contradicts them. Under the signed-direction convention, positive signed estimates for direction -1 mean stronger dependency in the exposed group, while positive signed estimates for direction +1 mean weaker dependency. The best supported dataset-specific associations are: KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency; SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, especially in TP53-intact cells; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. The first four major axes have independent validation and also appear robust across screen quality, Cas9 activity, and aneuploidy strata. PTEN-STAT3 is internally robust across many biological and assay contexts, but lacks independent validation and should be treated only as an association in this supplied dataset. Negative findings include direct-target dependency predictions that are near-null or below practical importance: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, MYC amplification with POLR2A/RPL11/DHX9/KIF18A/USP7/WRN dependency, RB1 loss with KIF18A/POLR2A/SMARCA2 dependency, NF1 loss with KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type contexts, and constructed markers D/E/F. Unresolved uncertainty remains for low-count or wide-interval interactions, especially CDKN2A-MDM2 effects under TP53 loss, high 9p21 copy number, batch, and MTAP interaction models, and for residual confounding of PTEN-STAT3 by media, culture, library, ploidy, omics completeness, batch, or screen noise. The most informative next analysis is to run the 12 active internal robustness comparisons: PTEN-STAT3 across media serum, adherent culture, non-Avana library, ploidy, matched RNA/DNA status, batch A, and a newly registered screen_nnmd restriction, plus low-aneuploidy TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 tests. These analyses cannot establish causality or external generalizability.

Iteration 22/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so the next discovery value comes from targeted robustness tests rather than broad null-target mining. The strongest supplied-dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency especially in TP53-intact cells, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. Several of these remain accepted after high-screen-quality, high-Cas9, aneuploidy, and PTEN-STAT3 media/culture/library robustness tests, but low-screen-quality strata have not yet been checked for four of the largest effects. I therefore register four low-screen_roc_auc refinements: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-loss USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency, and MSI-high WRN dependency in screens with screen_roc_auc at or below the median. Direction convention is unchanged: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger or more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker or less negative dependency. If these low-quality-screen estimates remain large and exclude zero, the accepted associations are less likely to be artifacts confined to high-quality screens. If they attenuate substantially, the claims remain association-level but require caution because assay-quality or screen-noise structure could contribute. I used an operational practical magnitude of roughly 0.10 dependency-score units for these compact CRISPR scores, along with interval exclusion of zero and valid cell counts. These proposals do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

H250-H257 are all accepted and closed: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency remains very large under high screen_roc_auc (+0.791 [0.764,0.819]), high Cas9 activity (+0.791 [0.759,0.823]), and low aneuploidy (+0.799 [0.759,0.838]); TP53-loss USP7 dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.806 [0.780,0.832]) and high Cas9 activity (+0.799 [0.768,0.829]); KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.793 [0.764,0.822]) and high aneuploidy (+0.796 [0.755,0.838]); and MSI-high WRN dependency remains very large under high screen quality (+0.790 [0.751,0.829]). Because PTEN-STAT3 remains accepted internally but lacks independent validation, this robustness to assay-quality and editing-efficiency strata strengthens it as a dataset-specific association, while still leaving open correlated biology, genetic co-occurrence, copy-number effects, or other residual confounders. record.narrative: Newly delivered discovery evidence assesses internal robustness of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency across media serum, adherent culture, ploidy strata, omics completeness, batch A, and a screen_nnmd stratum, plus low-aneuploidy strata for TP53-loss USP7 and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2. Under the signed-direction convention, all PTEN STAT3 claims are direction -1, so positive estimates indicate stronger, more negative STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells; TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 claims are direction +1, so positive estimates indicate weaker dependency in the exposed group. H262-H264 and H266-H270 are accepted because PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency remains around +0.22 to +0.29, intervals exclude zero, point estimates exceed the practical ~0.10 dependency-unit threshold, and cell counts are valid. This supports a dataset-specific association robust to common media, culture, ploidy, omics-completeness, and batch strata, but not causality or generalizability. H265 is unresolved and closed because the non-Avana-library stratum has only 27 PTEN-loss cells, interval crosses zero, and the point estimate is below the practical threshold; it neither confirms nor refutes attenuation in that assay context. H273 is accepted: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency remains +0.324 [0.247, 0.400] under the screen_nnmd criterion, adding screen-noise-related robustness. H271 and H272 are accepted with very large effects, +0.824 [0.783, 0.866] and +0.830 [0.792, 0.868], showing TP53-USP7 and KEAP1-NFE2L2 associations persist in low-aneuploidy cells. The main remaining concern is multiplicity in many subgroup tests, but these are planned robustness checks of already strong associations rather than new independent claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The final dataset-specific conclusion is that the strongest scientifically meaningful associations are: KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency H18 R5 +0.796 [0.776,0.816], independently validated R26 +0.781 [0.752,0.809]; TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency H12 R10 +0.802 [0.782,0.822], independently validated R13 +0.797 [0.769,0.824]; SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency H7 R7 +0.784 [0.765,0.803], independently validated R39 +0.807 [0.777,0.838]; MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency H13 R11 +0.790 [0.760,0.819], independently validated R53 +0.771 [0.720,0.822]; CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency, clearest in TP53-intact cells H96 R70 +0.119 [0.079,0.158], independently validated R93 +0.122 [0.064,0.180], with the overall estimate also supported H117 R108 +0.117 [0.082,0.152]; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency H184 R188 +0.267 [0.215,0.319]. PTEN-STAT3 lacks independent validation but is internally robust across many strata, including TP53 status, KRAS status, MYC expression, IFN and EMT signatures, high and low screen_roc_auc, serum, adherent culture, ploidy, omics completeness, batch A, and screen_nnmd examples R191, R192, R242, R247, R260, R263, R264, R265, R267, R269, R271, and R274. I used about 0.10 dependency-score units as a pragmatic meaningful magnitude, together with valid cell counts and interval exclusion of zero; the larger validated effects are far above this threshold, whereas near-null direct-target tests are well below it. Negative or nonmeaningful findings include direct target dependencies that are generally null or below practical importance: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency H1 R1 +0.014 [-0.004,0.031] and TP53-intact validated R80 +0.001 [-0.028,0.030]; BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency H2 R2 -0.017 [-0.045,0.012]; EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency H3 R3 +0.025 [-0.000,0.051] and TP53-intact validated H51 R133 -0.027 [-0.069,0.016]; ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency H4 R4 +0.001 [-0.027,0.030]. MYC amplification is not practically associated with POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, or WRN, including nominally significant but small WRN estimate R186 -0.033 [-0.064,-0.002]. RB1 loss is not practically associated with KIF18A or POLR2A; NF1 loss is not practically associated with KRAS dependency in KRAS-wild-type cells despite a small discovery effect R52 +0.039 [0.006,0.071] that was not validated R66 +0.000 [-0.042,0.043]; and constructed markers D/E/F show no meaningful dependency-score associations, with some nominal intervals excluding zero but estimates below the practical threshold. Unresolved uncertainty remains for low screen_roc_auc strata for SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and MSI-high-WRN, which are active but unanalyzed H274-H277. I registered two low screen_roc_auc CDKN2A-MDM2 tests and five low Cas9 activity tests as the next robustness analyses because assay quality may attenuate large dependency effects. CDKN2A-MDM2 in TP53-loss cells remains uncertain because overall TP53-loss validation R106 +0.101 [-0.000,0.202] is boundary-like and MTAP interaction tests are wide or insufficient; high 9p21 copy-number and batch strata are also uncertain because intervals are wide or exposed cells are small. PTEN-STAT3 remains association-only because independent validation is no longer possible and the non-Avana library test H265 R266 is underpowered. All conclusions are limited to the supplied 2000-line lung adenocarcinoma dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability. The most informative next step is to analyze H274-H277 plus the newly registered low screen-quality and low-Cas9 tests; persistence of intervals excluding zero and estimates at least about 0.10 would strengthen dataset-specific robustness, whereas attenuation or invalid cells would keep the claims association-level and raise assay-quality caution.

Iteration 23/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so the most useful exploration is to complete the internal assay-quality robustness battery. Active claims already cover low screen_roc_auc strata for the largest accepted associations, plus low screen_roc_auc CDKN2A-MDM2 tests and low Cas9 tests for SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, and TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2. The major accepted PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency association has already passed many robustness checks, including high Cas9, but has not been tested in low Cas9 activity. I register one refinement of H184: PTEN-loss versus PTEN-intact STAT3 dependency in cells with cas9_activity_pct at or below the lower quartile (67.7). Direction remains -1, so a positive signed estimate means stronger, more negative STAT3 dependency in PTEN-loss cells; the anticipated raw contrast is negative. I will regard persistence as support if the estimate is at least roughly 0.10 dependency-score units, the 95% Welch interval excludes zero, and every cell has at least 20 observations. Substantial attenuation, a wide interval, or insufficient cells would keep the PTEN-STAT3 association dataset-specific and raise concern that low perturbation efficiency or noisy screens contribute to the apparent effect. This single addition makes the active discovery pool approximately twelve claims, including low Cas9 PTEN-STAT3. These analyses assess association robustness within the supplied dataset only and cannot establish causality or external generalizability.

Iteration 23/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The claims cover the major accepted associations under low screen_roc_auc strata (H274-H279) and low Cas9-activity strata (H280-H285), completing the planned low-quality-screen and low-Cas9 checks for SMARCA4 loss-SMARCA2, TP53 loss-USP7, KEAP1 loss-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, CDKN2A loss-MDM2 including TP53-intact cells, and PTEN loss-STAT3. Under the signed-direction convention, direction -1 positive estimates mean stronger/more negative dependency in the exposed group; direction +1 positive estimates mean weaker/less negative dependency. I will require valid cells, intervals excluding zero, and estimates of at least roughly 0.10 dependency-score units to regard these associations as internally robust under degraded assay quality. Persistent effects would strengthen the dataset-specific conclusion; attenuation or invalid cells would keep the claims association-level and suggest sensitivity to screen noise or perturbation efficiency. These results remain noncausal and non-generalizable.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The twelve new discovery results complete the planned low screen_roc_auc and low Cas9-activity robustness battery for the main accepted dependency associations. All comparisons are valid by cell counts and are direction consistent with the parent claims. Under the signed convention, positive values mean stronger dependency for direction -1 claims and weaker dependency for direction +1 claims. The large SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, and PTEN-STAT3 associations persist with very large estimates in low screen-quality or low-Cas9 strata: roughly +0.75 to +0.83 for the first four families and +0.37 for PTEN-STAT3, all with intervals excluding zero. This supports dataset-specific internal robustness to degraded screen discrimination or perturbation efficiency, but it does not imply causality or external generalizability. The CDKN2A-MDM2 effects in low screen_roc_auc and low-Cas9 strata are smaller and more uncertain: point estimates are around +0.103 and +0.105, intervals exclude zero, but lower bounds are below the pragmatic 0.10 dependency-unit guideline and are wide. I therefore accept these as dataset-specific positive associations under degraded assay quality, with explicit caution that low screen quality and low Cas9 activity may attenuate precision and magnitude. H283 has only 27 exposed cells but a huge WRN effect with an interval excluding zero; it is accepted as internally robust but should be read cautiously because of its small exposed subset. H285 shows PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency remains strong in low Cas9 activity, closing the remaining low-Cas9 robustness question. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request can be made. To complete an analogous low screen_nnmd battery, I registered refinements testing the major accepted associations in the lower quartile of screen_nnmd, including PTEN-STAT3, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, overall CDKN2A-MDM2, and TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2. These remain association-level internal robustness checks only.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

record.narrative: No new validation response is due and independent validation capacity is exhausted. The final synthesis therefore assesses the accumulated discovery and prior validation evidence for the supplied 2000-sample lung adenocarcinoma-like dataset. Because dependency scores are continuous with standard deviations about 0.18-0.26, I treated roughly 0.10 dependency-score units (about 0.4-0.5 SD for many scores) together with valid Welch cells and interval exclusion of zero as scientifically meaningful, consistent with the stated 10% practical threshold. Signed estimates follow the registered hypothesis direction. Supported dataset-specific associations. KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H18/H5; R5 +0.796 [0.776,0.816], validated R26 +0.781 [0.752,0.809]) and persists in low screen_roc_auc (R277) and low Cas9 strata (R283). TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency (H12; R10 +0.802 [0.782,0.822], validated R13 +0.797 [0.769,0.824]), robust in low screen_roc_auc (R276) and low Cas9 strata (R282). SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H7; R7 +0.784 [0.765,0.803], validated R39 +0.807 [0.777,0.838]), robust in low screen_roc_auc (R275) and low Cas9 strata (R281). MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H13; R11 +0.790 [0.760,0.819], validated R53 +0.771 [0.720,0.822]), including adenocarcinoma subtype (H24; R23/R40), low screen_roc_auc (R278), and low Cas9 strata (R284), though the latter has only 27 exposed cells and is accepted with caution. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, clearest in TP53-intact cells (H96; R70 +0.119 [0.079,0.158], validated R93 +0.122 [0.064,0.180]) and overall (H117; R108 +0.117 [0.082,0.152]); low screen_roc_auc and low Cas9 checks remain positive but attenuated (H278 R279 +0.103, H279 R280 +0.106, H284 R285 +0.105), with lower bounds often below 0.10, so magnitude in degraded-quality subsets is uncertain. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H184; R188 +0.267 [0.215,0.319]); although independently validated PTEN-STAT3 has not been obtained because validation capacity is exhausted, the association is internally robust across many strata, including TP53 status, KRAS status, MYC expression, IFN and EMT signatures, ploidy, media, culture, omics completeness, batch A, low screen_roc_auc, and low Cas9 (H285; R286 +0.372 [0.268,0.476]). Negative or non-meaningful findings. Direct target associations are generally null or far below the practical threshold: KRAS mutation with dependency_KRAS (H1; R1 +0.014 [-0.004,0.031], validated R80 +0.001), BRAF V600E with dependency_BRAF (H2; R2 -0.017), EGFR amplification with dependency_EGFR (H3; R3 +0.025 and validated H51/R133 -0.027), and ERBB2 amplification with dependency_ERBB2 (H4; R4 +0.001). MYC amplification is not practically associated with POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, or WRN; the nominally significant WRN effect (R186 -0.033 [-0.064,-0.002]) is small. RB1 loss is not practically associated with KIF18A or POLR2A, NF1 loss fails independent validation for dependency_KRAS in KRAS-wild-type cells (R52 discovery +0.039, R66 validation +0.000), MTAP loss is not a robust modifier of CDKN2A-MDM2, and high/low copy_number_9p21 or batch strata are wide or boundary-like. Constructed research markers D/E/F and signatures A/B/C show no meaningful dependency associations beyond nominal small effects; some intervals exclude zero but point estimates are below 0.10. Unresolved uncertainty. The main remaining registered active evidence gap is the low screen_nnmd robustness battery H286-H292, which has no evidence yet. These include PTEN-STAT3, SMARCA4-SMARCA2, TP53-USP7, KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, overall CDKN2A-MDM2, and TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 in lower-quartile screen_nnmd. Additional unresolved or bounded uncertainty concerns CDKN2A-MDM2 effects in TP53-loss or MTAP/9p21 interactions (e.g., H108 validation R106 lower bound approximately zero), non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 (H265 underpowered), and small or nominal interaction estimates. PTEN-STAT3 remains accepted only as a robust association within the supplied data, not as externally validated or causal. Most informative next analysis is to run the active low screen_nnmd battery H286-H292. Persistence of intervals excluding zero with estimates at least about 0.10 would further strengthen dataset-specific robustness across degraded screen noise; attenuation or invalid cells would keep the claims association-level and specify that screen noise can limit inference. All accepted claims should be interpreted as associations within this single supplied lung adenocarcinoma-like dataset, not as causal mechanisms or generalizable clinical biology.

Iteration 24/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: These twelve results complete the screen_nnmd quartile robustness battery for the main accepted dependency associations. Under the signed convention, positive estimates for direction -1 claims mean stronger dependency in exposed cells, and positive estimates for direction +1 claims mean weaker dependency in exposed cells. The very large-effect families remain directionally and practically robust in both lower and upper screen_nnmd quartiles: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (+0.807 low, +0.766 high), TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency (+0.815 low, +0.797 high), KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (+0.779 low, +0.808 high), MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency (+0.794 low, +0.821 high), and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency (+0.238 low, lower bound 0.128, above the practical 0.10 dependency-unit threshold). I accept these as dataset-specific internal robustness evidence, not causality or external generalizability. The MSI-high WRN strata have small exposed subsets (37 and 24 cells), but the effects are enormous and their intervals remain far from zero, so acceptance is reasonable with explicit caution. The CDKN2A-MDM2 screen_nnmd refinements are less decisive: low-quartile overall CDKN2A loss gives +0.095 [0.021,0.169], TP53-intact low quartile gives +0.074 [-0.010,0.158], and TP53-intact high quartile gives +0.087 [0.023,0.152]. The two intervals excluding zero remain below my practical 0.10 dependency-unit robustness benchmark, and the TP53-intact low-quartile interval crosses zero. I therefore leave these specific screen_nnmd refinements unresolved rather than accepting them as scientifically meaningful stratum-specific effects. This does not overturn the parent CDKN2A-MDM2 association, which remains accepted from broader and independently validated evidence; it specifies that the smaller CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is uncertain at screen-noise extremes. Multiplicity was not adjusted, but the planned battery is now complete and the very large effects are not plausibly artifacts of testing many comparisons, while the borderline CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates should not be overinterpreted. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request is possible.

Iteration 24/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
