record.narrative:
No new validation response is due and independent validation capacity is exhausted. This synthesis therefore reports the final scientific interpretation of the supplied 2000-sample lung-lineage dataset. Signed estimates follow the registered hypothesis direction; positive values mean the supported direction in the signed claim. I treated roughly 0.10 dependency-score units, valid Welch cells, interval exclusion of zero, and where available independent validation as scientifically meaningful. All conclusions are associations within this supplied dataset only; they are not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable clinical biology.

Supported dataset-specific associations. (1) KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency: R5 +0.796 [0.776,0.816], independently validated by R26 +0.781 [0.752,0.809]; the effect persists in adenocarcinoma, TP53-loss and TP53-intact, KRAS-mutant, EGFR-amplified, MSI-high, aneuploid, lower screen_roc_auc, lower Cas9, and both screen_nnmd quartiles. (2) TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency: R10 +0.802 [0.782,0.822], validated R13 +0.797 [0.769,0.824], robust across adenocarcinoma, KRAS, aneuploidy, screen-quality strata, and screen_nnmd extremes. (3) SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: R7 +0.784 [0.765,0.803], validated R39 +0.807 [0.777,0.838]; this holds in ARID1A-intact and ARID1A-loss cells, adenocarcinoma, many screen-quality strata, and screen_nnmd extremes, with only small residual batch heterogeneity. (4) MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: R11 +0.790 [0.760,0.819], validated R53 +0.771 [0.720,0.822]; also adenocarcinoma, higher mutation burden, BRCA2-intact, ploidy/hypoxia/screen-quality checks, and screen_nnmd extremes. Some MSI strata have small exposed cell counts, but effects are very large and intervals remain far from zero. (5) PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: R188 +0.267 [0.215,0.319]. Although independent validation capacity was exhausted before PTEN-STAT3 could be validated, the association is internally robust across TP53, KRAS, MYC expression, IFN-gamma, hypoxia, EMT, ploidy, media, culture, matched-omics availability, batch A, screen quality, and screen_nnmd quartiles. (6) CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, clearest in TP53-intact cells: R70 +0.119 [0.079,0.158], validated R93 +0.122 [0.064,0.180]; the full-population estimate is R108 +0.117 [0.082,0.152]. This is accepted as a real but smaller dataset-specific association, with magnitude uncertainty in some degraded-quality or small subgroups.

Subgroups and effect modifiers. The very large associations above show little meaningful interaction by lineage subtype, TP53/KEAP1 coalteration, or screen quality in the planned tests; small nominally significant heterogeneity such as batch effects on SMARCA4-SMARCA2 or stratum-specific CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates should not be overinterpreted. The accepted subgroup findings mostly reinforce the same main associations rather than identify distinct biology. MTAP loss, 9p21 copy-number extremes, and constructed research markers/signatures D/E/F and signatures A/B/C did not yield robust, biologically interpretable modifiers at the practical effect threshold.

Negative or non-meaningful findings. Direct target alteration associations were generally null or far below practical importance: KRAS mutation with dependency_KRAS (R1 +0.014 [-0.004,0.031], validated R80 +0.001 [-0.028,0.030]), BRAF V600E with dependency_BRAF (R2 -0.017 [-0.045,0.012]), EGFR amplification with dependency_EGFR (R3 +0.025 [-0.0003,0.051], validated signed estimate -0.027 [-0.069,0.016]), and ERBB2 amplification with dependency_ERBB2 (R4 +0.001 [-0.027,0.030]). MYC amplification was not practically associated with POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, or WRN; the nominally significant WRN absolute magnitude was about 0.033. RB1 loss did not practically track KIF18A or POLR2A. NF1 loss initially tracked dependency_KRAS in KRAS-wildtype cells (R52 +0.039 [0.006,0.071]) but failed validation (R66 +0.000 [-0.042,0.043]). TP53 loss did not support MDM2/RPL11 hypotheses as expected, MTAP loss did not robustly modify CDKN2A-MDM2 (R103 validation direction reversed), and small interaction or small-cell stratum claims remain non-priority.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main accepted findings are strong enough that multiplicity and nominal testing do not plausibly explain them. Remaining uncertainty is mainly for small or subgroup-specific effects. In the completed screen_nnmd robustness battery, CDKN2A-MDM2 estimates at screen-noise extremes were borderline: low quartile overall +0.095 [0.021,0.169], TP53-intact low +0.074 [-0.010,0.158], TP53-intact high +0.087 [0.023,0.152]. These do not overturn the parent CDKN2A-MDM2 association, but they do not establish practical screen-noise-stratum effects. PTEN-STAT3 lacks independent validation and remains underpowered in non-Avana-library cells. Some interactions by MTAP, 9p21, or batch are wide or boundary-like.

Next analysis and final conclusion. Since validation capacity is exhausted, the most informative next discovery analyses are registered subtype-interaction checks for the internally robust but unvalidated PTEN-STAT3 association and for TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2. A near-zero lineage interaction with tight intervals would strengthen internal generalization across subtypes; a meaningful positive interaction would restrict those associations to adenocarcinoma. Overall, the evidence supports six dataset-specific dependency associations: KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, TP53-loss/USP7, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, PTEN-loss/STAT3, and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2, with direct target dependencies and constructed marker effects largely negative. These should be interpreted as patterns of association in this supplied dataset, not as causal mechanisms or clinically generalizable biomarkers.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so the final exploration should prioritize discovery-stage tests that maximize information about the two accepted associations that lack independent validation: PTEN-loss/STAT3 and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 in TP53-intact cells. I register eight new direction -1 interaction hypotheses. For CDKN2A comparisons, the eligible population is TP53-loss absent; for PTEN comparisons, eligibility is unrestricted. The subgroup comparisons test whether the exposed-minus-comparator association is stronger in adenocarcinoma, higher ploidy, high-serum media, or high screen_roc_auc than in the corresponding complement. These modifiers are scientifically useful because they test whether the unvalidated PTEN-STAT3 effect is subtype-restricted or stable across aneuploidy, growth-context, and screen-quality strata, and whether the smaller CDKN2A-MDM2 effect is stable rather than driven by particular contexts. Under the signed convention for direction -1, a positive signed interaction estimate means the exposed effect is stronger, i.e. more negative dependency in the named subgroup, whereas a negative signed estimate means attenuation or reversal relative to the complement. I expect adenocarcinoma effects to be at least as strong for both associations; for ploidy, serum, and screen-quality interactions I expect approximately null effect modification because prior high/low stratum estimates were already broadly concordant. I will regard a modifier as scientifically meaningful only if the 95% Welch interval excludes zero and the absolute signed magnitude is practically large; as a conservative guideline I use at least about 0.10 dependency-score units for the larger PTEN effect and about 0.05-0.10 for the smaller CDKN2A effect, noting that both correspond to more than a 10% relative shift on these dependency-score scales. Tight intervals near zero support internal generalization across these measured contexts; wide intervals or small-cell invalidity will be interpreted as unresolved effect modification, not as overturning the parent main association. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and are not causal or externally generalizable.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this final analysis slot should spend all available discovery analyses on the most informative registered comparisons: the planned effect-modifier/robustness interactions for the two main accepted dataset-specific associations that lack independent validation, namely PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency and CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells. I request eight direction -1 interaction claims: H300 and H301 for adenocarcinoma, H302 and H303 for ploidy >= median, H304 and H305 for media_serum_pct >= 10, and H306 and H307 for screen_roc_auc >= median. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator association in the named subgroup against its complement within the same eligible population. For the direction -1 interaction claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed association is stronger in the named subgroup than in the complement; a negative signed estimate means attenuation or reversal. I will regard an interaction as scientifically meaningful only if all Welch cells are valid, the 95% interval excludes zero, and the signed magnitude is practically large: roughly at least 0.10 dependency-score units for the larger PTEN-STAT3 association and around 0.05-0.10 for the smaller TP53-intact CDKN2A-MDM2 association. Tight intervals near zero will be interpreted as supporting internal robustness across these measured contexts, not as evidence of effect modification. To avoid duplicate no-new-sample tests of the same raw lineage interaction under opposite signs, I defer H298 and H299 and use H300 and H301 as the primary signed lineage-interaction claims. All requested tests are dataset-specific association analyses, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Iteration 25/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

record.narrative: All eight newly delivered interaction results are valid Welch comparisons with every cell above the minimum n, and they use measured predictors rather than outcome-derived exposures, so there is no obvious leakage. Under the signed convention, a positive interaction means the exposed-minus-comparator association is stronger in the named subgroup than in its complement, whereas a negative interaction means attenuation or reversal.
